3314: It follows the same path as Flowchart 2 and adds questions about the body, thoughts and emotions:
3315: Do I feel stress, anxiety or overload? Can I step away from where I am for a few minutes? If so, I take a micro-break; if not, I use a strategy on the spot (controlled breathing, 5-4-3-2-1 grounding or STOP).
3316: Is my body still very activated? If so: mindfulness, attentional focus or light physical activation.
3317: If not, I notice what is most present. Racing or repetitive thoughts: STOP, putting worries outside myself or attentional focus. Physical tension: light physical activation or muscle relaxation. Emotional overload or isolation: touch, talking to someone I trust or normalising the experience.
3318: Do I already feel calmer or more in control? If so, I go back to a simple task (one small, concrete step). If not, I choose another strategy or repeat the earlier ones, look at Module 6 and seek help.

3402: Faced with a sudden, serious or potentially traumatic event, intense stress reactions are to be expected. Psychological First Aid aims to reduce immediate distress, promote safety and support early recovery. At Benfica, it may be a serious incident at the Stadium with spectators present (a fall, a sudden illness, an evacuation), an accident at work or tragic news that affects the whole club.

3415: 5.8 Supporting a member or fan in distress
3417: Supporting a member or fan in distress
3418: A member, fan or visitor in emotional distress may be more sensitive, more reactive or find it harder to express their needs in an organised way. This can happen at the Stadium gates, at the ticket office, in the store, at the Museum or on the phone, and on a matchday the emotion of the result can amplify what the person is already carrying. The aim is not to do psychotherapy, but to offer a human, safe and empathetic response within the professional role.
3419: A colleague hands a box to a customer, smiling.
3420: The member, fan or visitor may be going through emotionally demanding personal or professional situations, and may show:
3421: frustration with the service (tickets, membership fees, queues, access)
3422: Illustration: two people standing, talking calmly.
3423: An employee attends to two people attentively.
3424: Show availability: Listen actively and respectfully, showing genuine interest in what the person is communicating.
3425: Clarify needs: Use open, non-intrusive questions to understand what happened, what the person needs and how they can be helped at that moment.
3426: Use stabilisation strategies: If the person is very dysregulated: encourage slow breathing, use grounding, help them bring their attention back to the present.
3427: Trying to “fix” the distress straight away: The pressure to make the person feel better quickly can reduce the capacity for genuine listening.

3465: Code of Conduct and whistleblowing channel
3466: The Benfica SAD Code of Conduct (in force since 23 November 2022) states that the physical and psychological well-being of the people who work at Benfica is of fundamental importance. It prohibits harassment and discrimination at work and protects those who report it.
3467: Among other things, degrading or humiliating comments, intimidating or threatening behaviour, and ignoring, isolating or excluding a colleague are unacceptable
3468: Anyone who knows of or has well-founded suspicions of harassment must report it
3469: Those who report it, and the witnesses they name, cannot be disciplined for doing so, unless they acted in bad faith
3470: Internal, confidential whistleblowing channel: slbenficasad.integrityline.com (opens in a new window)
3472: (Information not available in this demo version) This is the Benfica SAD Code. Confirm whether the same code and the same channel apply to all employees of the Club and of the other entities of the Benfica Group.
3473: All workers are entitled to Occupational Medicine, in addition to the mandatory periodic check-ups:
3474: These appointments can be requested through Human Resources or the Occupational Health and Safety service. (Information not available in this demo version) At very busy times, such as weeks with several matches, it may not be possible to get an appointment on the same day.
3475: If Occupational Medicine cannot respond within the expected time, an appropriate alternative should be activated (e.g. the internal employee support line (Information not available in this demo version), SNS 24 – 808 24 24 24, option 4 –, psychological support or an external resource), so that the response to the employee is not delayed.
